title: An AI model is not the same as an app
summary: Separate the engine, the interface and the tools before choosing where to work.
outcome: Explain why the same model can behave differently in different apps.

sections.title: Start with the distinction
sections.body:
A model is a trained system that maps an input to an output. An app is the experience around that model: a message box, file uploads, search, saved conversations and other controls. An API is a way for software to request a model’s output. They are related, but they are not interchangeable.

- ChatGPT is an app; OpenAI provides models and developer services.
- Claude is both a product family and a model family. The Claude app and its developer Console are different workspaces.
- Gemini has a consumer app; Google AI Studio is a developer experimentation surface.
- Grok and DeepSeek also distinguish user-facing chat from developer APIs.

sections.title: What the model actually receives
sections.body:
The response depends on the instructions, conversation, selected files and tool results that the app includes in the request. A file existing somewhere in your account does not guarantee the model can see it. Ask for the source passage and check it yourself.

A search tool can fetch information outside model training. A calculator or code tool can perform a calculation. The model’s fluent wording alone is not proof that either tool ran.

sections.title: Choose for the work
sections.body:
For a first draft, begin with an ordinary chat. For evidence from a document, use a source-based workflow. For current external facts, use a supported search or research feature and inspect the sources. For an action such as sending a message, keep a human approval point.

Try one small task in two available apps. Compare correctness, source traceability and the work you had to do to repair the result—not just the length of the response.
